sentences.text: As both the petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 14.01.2024 at about 5.10 p.m., the petitioner in MVC No.775/2024 (as a rider) and petitioner in MVC No.774/2024 (as a pillion rider) were proceeding on a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KF-2907 slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached Opposite to AMC College, Kalkere, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-37-CQ-6073 was going ahead of the petitioners motorcycle in the same direction, with high speed in rash and negligent manner without showing any signal all of a sudden applied brake and stopped and then to swered his vehicle towards left side of the road as a result the rider / petitioner in MVC.775/2024 could not control his vehicle and dashed to the hind portion of the Lorry.

Due to the said impact, both the rider and pillion rider Sharath Kumar Y vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86650889/

Anyhow the rider / petitioner in MVC.774/2024 being under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident, by itself would not lead to an automatic inference that he contributed to the cause of accident as a matter of course.

But what cannot be overlooked is that if a person drives a vehicle after taking alcohol and being under its influence, he is likely to expose Sharath Kumar Y vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86650889/

sentences.text: To put it differently, a drunken driver is a potential murderer as he cannot perform his tasks without risks and endangers road safety.
This is so because after drinking, the judgment power of the driver gets impaired due to which he tends to take more risks, becomes more aggressive and takes a longer reaction time.
But in the present case on hand no allegations against the rider of the motorcycle as he was under influence of alcohol and he is also reason for caused the accident.
Hence the contentions urged by the respondent No.1 does not hold any water in the eye of law.
13. The respondent No.1 further contended that lorry not involved in the accident.

It is pertinent to note that IO has given  11  SCCH-23  MVC.774/2024 C/w MVC.775/2024 Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P6 and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.7 wherein the owner of the offending lorry has admitted the involvement of the vehicle.
Mere taking up of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the evidence led by the petitioners.
Further the respondents did not make any attempt to examine the driver of the insured vehicle who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the driver of the insured vehicle is fatal to the defence of the respondent No.1.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of Lorry.
